title: Super Fast: Haloumi Couscous Salad
subtitle: On the table in under 20 minutes!
description: Five easy steps, minimal pans and prep… we cut the fluff but not the flavour in our 'super-fast' recipes. In just 20 minutes, you’ll have this masterpiece on the table and be crowned in glory too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Shred the carrot using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Quarter the zucchini lengthwise, then cut into 1cm chunks. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Thinly slice the haloumi.

Soak couscous: Put the couscous in a large heatproof bowl, pour over 200ml boiling water and cover with a plate. Stand for 5 mins or until the water is absorbed. Season with salt and pepper, then fluff the couscous with a fork.

Soften veggies: Meanwhile, heat a drizzle of olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the zucchini, stirring, for 5 mins or until slightly softened. Add the carrot and garlic and cook, stirring, for 2 mins. Add half the Moroccan seasoning and cook, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Remove from the pan, reserving the pan.

Cook haloumi: Combine the remaining Moroccan seasoning and a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large bowl. Add the haloumi, season with salt and pepper and turn to coat. Heat the reserved pan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 2 mins each side or until golden. Remove from the pan.

Serve up: Put 3 tsp olive oil, 3 tsp red wine vinegar and 1½ tsp honey in a large bowl, season with salt and pepper and whisk to combine. Add the currants, spinach, veggies and couscous and toss to combine. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the couscous salad and haloumi among bowls and enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
